correctness.rationale: The integral binomial shuffle identity verifies the Zinbiel product in all characteristics. For n<=p, all relevant leading binomials are units, so ranks of h-th powers of each multiplication hand are max(n-hd,0). At n=p+1 only e_1 o e_p survives in top degree; a separate case analysis gives left J_(p+1), right J_p+J_1 for d=1, equal J_p^d+J_1 for 2<=d<=p-1, left zero/right rank-one for d=p, and both zero for d=p+1. The precise rank-power sequences determine all Jordan types; disjoint first-nonzero-coordinate strata have (q-1)q^(n-d) or q elements, giving the polynomial. The proof addresses p=2 and every field extension. The actual checker independently computes original multiplication matrices and all power ranks for 11 exhaustive plus 3 sampled field/dimension cases, including GF(4), GF(8), GF(9). Sampling is supporting evidence, not infinite proof.

The literature statements actually inspected are over complex scalars or about unrelated operator classes, so their mathematical conclusions do not assert the mod-p missing-rank event, the asymmetric annihilator jump, nor the exact joint finite-field distribution. originality.rationale: The original 2007 complex null-filiform multiplication table is fully acknowledged as prior art. The assessed novel statement is an all-element, two-sided positive-characteristic Jordan/rank census at and before the first modular cutoff n=p+1, including an exact finite-field polynomial, a one-sided annihilator jump, and rank-flag geometry. Direct comparison with the inspected complex classification papers, Sage shuffle rule, relevant mathematical findings, and specific literature searches found no equivalent or dominating theorem. A potential hidden modular divided-power/operator formulation remains a residual historical risk. Turemuratova (2026) is credited for the three-dimensional characteristic-two handed-annihilator example, so that particular observation is not presented as novel. Its full six-page article and Alvarez et al. (2022) lack the complete all-prime joint Jordan/rank census and uniform polynomial.
residual_risks: An unlocated equivalent modular Jordan-normal-form or divided-power operator result could subsume the claim under different terminology.
Known binomial structural coefficients make the census derivable; novelty is restricted to the completed first-cutoff two-hand classification and count, not those coefficients.
Historical comparison was self-review and cannot certify exhaustive priority.

A previously published three-dimensional characteristic-two example already shows unequal left/right annihilators; the general first-modular statement does not claim novelty for that particular example.

value.rationale: The cutoff n=p+1 is the first natural modular binomial degeneration for this canonical one-generator Zinbiel family. A complete two-handed Jordan census, exact joint rank polynomial, missing left rank, asymmetric annihilator jump, and nested coordinate-rank stratification distinguish it from a routine small-case rank computation. This fully resolves a natural structural invariant up to the first modular threshold for every prime and finite field, without claiming a general theorem for larger dimensions. The original multiplication table and characteristic-zero classifications are explicitly credited.
